title: dedicated: autoscaler burst & throughput reporting enhancement v2
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: customers running Dedicated fleets reported recurring burst throttling and unstable scaling decisions during short high-QPS windows; existing token-bucket smoothing made it hard to correlate committed throughput vs observed utilization in the Console. Motivation: provide clearer throughput guarantees, smoother burst controls, and richer utilization reporting so SREs and platform teams can tune commitments and detect regressions. This PR implements the next iteration of the dedicated autoscaler reporting and smoothing work (v2): - Add a throughput_guarantee parameter to fleet configs and surface expected vs achieved throughput in metrics and Console. - Improve token-bucket smoothing to reduce oscillations when short bursts spike (configurable smoothing window + decay). - Emit new utilization metrics: dedicated_fleet/allocated_tokens, dedicated_fleet/consumed_tokens, dedicated_fleet/throughput_achieved, dedicated_fleet/throughput_target. - Add a derived metric dedicated_fleet/burst_throttle_events and a histogram for queueing latency to help troubleshoot tail latency during throttles. - Wire metrics into the Console dashboard with a small telemetry panel and alert hints. - Add unit + integration tests and a small e2e scenario in perf-canary. Checklist:
- [x] token-bucket smoothing algorithm update (core autoscaler)
- [x] metrics instrumentation + migration notes
- [x] Console dashboard wiring and small UI panel
- [x] unit tests for smoothing edgecases
- [x] integration test simulating burst followed by sustained throughput
- [x] documented Linear links and release notes in PR body
Notes: This is intentionally additive and backward compatible: fleets that do not set throughput_guarantee continue to use heuristics. Admins can enable the new smoothing via fleet policy. Related: ENG-1421 (customer investigation), ENG-2103 (autoscaler telemetry roadmap).

release_notes: Add throughput_guarantee config for Dedicated fleets; improved token-bucket smoothing to reduce scaling oscillations; new metrics (allocated_tokens, consumed_tokens, throughput_target, throughput_achieved, burst_throttle_events) and Console panel to visualize committed vs achieved throughput. Backward compatible: existing fleets unchanged unless throughput_guarantee is set.
